content.title: Inotropes and vasopressors for acute heart failure / cardiogenic shock
content.summary: Multiple studies and a meta-analysis support use of norepinephrine as first-line vasopressor/vasoactive agent compared with dopamine or epinephrine in patients with cardiogenic shock. Dopamine was associated with more arrhythmic events and greater mortality in cardiogenic shock (but not in hypovolaemic or septic shock). Trials comparing epinephrine with norepinephrine reported higher incidence of refractory shock, higher heart rate and lactic acidosis with epinephrine. A meta-analysis (n≈2583) showed about a three-fold increase in risk of death with epinephrine versus norepinephrine in cardiogenic shock. Limitations include small sample sizes, limited revascularization data, and lack of detailed dose/duration information.

notable_trials_and_findings.finding: Trial comparing dopamine vs norepinephrine as first-line vasopressor
notable_trials_and_findings.details: Included 1679 patients; more arrhythmic events and greater mortality with dopamine in cardiogenic shock; significance seen in subgroup of ~280 patients with cardiogenic shock (fewer than 10% had MI).

notable_trials_and_findings.finding: Randomized trial epinephrine vs norepinephrine in cardiogenic shock due to acute MI
notable_trials_and_findings.details: Stopped prematurely because of higher incidence of refractory shock with epinephrine; epinephrine associated with higher heart rate and lactic acidosis.
Included ~2583 patients; reported ~three-fold increase in risk of death with epinephrine compared with norepinephrine.

evidence_summary.limitations: Heterogeneity in revascularization data, dose and duration details often missing, relatively small sample sizes in some trials, results partly exploratory.
